what: What Exchange gets for a series' stored zone, and what a Windows zone id read from Exchange means — the answers crates/adapter-ews/src/windows_tz.rs must give.
why: Exchange names a series' zone by a Windows id, the rest of Aperio by tzdata. The translation decides whether a series reaches Exchange with its clock, with another city's, or with none, and what a series from Outlook repeats on. A hand-kept table had drifted: three wrong rows, and 174 of the 312 listed zones written without a zone.
decidedBy: DESIGN-series-time-zone.md, stage 4, and decisions 14a (no zone repeats in UTC), 22a (zones Exchange cannot store), 25b (a merged place is stored as its target) and 26a (one rule for zones).
writtenBy: By hand, from the CLDR release-48-2 windowsZones.xml pinned in crates/adapter-ews/cldr/ and from tzdata 2025b. Chosen, not measured: each row pins one reason the rule exists. The generated table they are checked against is crates/adapter-ews/src/windows_tz/windows_zones.rs.
readBy: crates/adapter-ews/src/windows_tz.rs (the `every_contract_row_holds` test; its MUST_RUN list names every row)

shape.write: [{name, tzid, expect, note}]: tzid is the series' stored zone or null; expect is {id} (StartTimeZone and EndTimeZone with this id), {no_zone: true}, or {not_storable: no_windows_zone | other_clock, windows?}
shape.read: [{name, windows, expect, note}]: windows is the StartTimeZone Id Exchange reports; expect is {zone}, {utc: true} or {unknown: true}

write.name: berlin-default
write.note: The default zone of its id.

write.name: vienna-member
write.note: Another city under the same id: the hand table once wrote Vienna without a zone.

write.name: lowercase-berlin
write.note: Any ASCII case, as the core resolves it.

write.name: device-spelling-calcutta
write.note: The spelling WebView2 reports resolves through the core first; the hand table wrote no zone.

write.name: merged-oslo
write.note: A merged place writes its target's id (25b).

write.name: merged-amsterdam-takes-brussels
write.note: CLDR files Amsterdam under W. Europe, but tzdata merged it into Brussels, which CLDR files under Romance: the stored target's id wins (25b). Same clock since 1970.

write.name: merged-copenhagen-takes-berlin
write.note: The other way round: CLDR files Copenhagen under Romance, its target Berlin under W. Europe.

write.name: kyiv-only-through-kiev
write.note: CLDR still spells it Europe/Kiev; the zone takes the one id its spellings agree on.

write.name: kanton-through-enderbury
write.note: Only CLDR's old name Pacific/Enderbury is in the file.

write.name: chihuahua-cldr43
write.note: CLDR 43 moved it after Mexico's 2022 change; the hand table wrote Mountain Standard Time (Mexico). The CLDR row ends in a space.

write.name: almaty-cldr45
write.note: Kazakhstan went to +05:00 in 2024 and CLDR 45 followed; the hand table wrote Central Asia Standard Time.

write.name: beirut-middle-east
write.note: The hand table wrote Lebanon Standard Time, which is not a Windows id at all.

write.name: coyhaique-cldr48
write.note: A zone tzdata 2025b added, which CLDR 48 files.

write.name: etc-gmt-minus-1
write.note: A fixed offset follows its CLDR row, on the same clock.

write.name: troll-no-windows-zone
write.note: The one listed zone CLDR has no id for (22a).

write.name: scoresbysund-other-clock
write.note: CLDR files it under the Azores' id, but since 2024 it runs -02:00/-01:00 and the Azores -01:00/+00:00: Exchange would store another clock (22a).

write.name: utc-name-utc
write.note: A UTC name is no zone (26a); the hand table wrote Id="UTC" for five of the eighteen spellings.

write.name: utc-name-gmt
write.note: Another UTC name.

write.name: utc-name-etc-zulu
write.note: Another UTC name.

write.name: unknown-name
write.note: A name tzdata does not know repeats in UTC (26a).

write.name: offset-string
write.note: An offset is not a tzdata name.

write.name: padded-berlin
write.note: The core does not trim: a padded name is not a zone.

write.name: no-tzid
write.note: A series without a zone.

read.name: w-europe-berlin
read.note: An id reads as its default zone.

read.name: india-kolkata
read.note: CLDR's default Asia/Calcutta, in tzdata's canonical spelling.

read.name: fle-kyiv
read.note: CLDR's default Europe/Kiev, canonical; the hand table read Europe/Kiev.

read.name: greenwich-abidjan
read.note: CLDR's default Atlantic/Reykjavik is merged into Abidjan (25b). Aperio writes the same id as the end zone; any end zone but the no-zone marker leaves the start id to decide.

read.name: greenwich-created-without-zone
read.note: Live test A2: Exchange 2019 stores a series created without a zone with this start and end zone. The end zone means no zone (43b).

read.name: utc-end-zone-in-any-case
read.note: The end marker is read in any ASCII case, and it wins over the start zone.

read.name: utc-is-no-zone
read.note: The UTC id is no zone; the hand table read Etc/UTC.

read.name: utc-minus-02-etc
read.note: A UTC-offset id reads as its fixed offset, a zone of its own.

read.name: mountain-mexico-mazatlan
read.note: CLDR 43 made Mazatlan the default; the hand table read Chihuahua.

read.name: central-asia-bishkek
read.note: CLDR 45 made Bishkek the default; the hand table read Almaty.

read.name: middle-east-beirut
read.note: One of 31 ids the hand table did not read, so such series repeated in UTC.

read.name: kamchatka-registry-only
read.note: In the Windows registry, not in CLDR.

read.name: lebanon-not-an-id
read.note: The id the hand table invented.
